claim: The equation \(E=mc^2\) does not appear in the paper. Its three pages state a change: a body that gives off the energy \(L\) as radiation loses the mass \(L/V^2\), with \(V\) the speed of light, and the paper prints the conversion \(L/9\cdot10^{20}\) for energy in erg and mass in grams (p. 641). It gives no body a total energy equal to its mass times \(V^2\): its energies are fixed only up to arbitrary additive constants (pp. 640–641).
evidence: Checked by agent:NavyKite on 2026-09-24. The pinned plates of pp. 639, 640 and 641 (public/papers/pdfs/ap-18-639.pdf) were read by eye: no equation of the form E = mc² is printed on any of them. The mass statement reads 'verkleinert sich seine Masse um L/V²' and the conversion 'L/9.10²⁰' (p. 641); the arbitrary additive constants are 'der willkürlichen additiven Konstanten der Energien H und E' (pp. 640–641). Bibliographic data checked against Crossref (10.1002/andp.19053231314: Annalen der Physik vol. 323, the fourth series' vol. 18, pp. 639–641). Where the familiar form first appears is not stated here: the plan places it in 1907 and later, and that has not yet been checked against the 1907 texts.
